extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, proprietors, representatives, patent attorneys, and European Patent Office staff involved in European patent filing and prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing Regulations to the European Patent Convention governing EPO procedures (languages, organisation, entitlement, filing, divisional applications, registration of transfers/licenses, oppositions/appeals, filings and formal requirements). Useful for applicants and representatives preparing and prosecuting European patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derogations — written proceedings language
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents and third parties intervening in opposition proceedings may file documents in any of the official languages of the European Patent Office; documents used as evidence (particularly publications) may be filed in any language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO may require a translation to one of its official languages within a time limit of not less than one month. If a translation must be filed under Article 14(2) it must be filed within three months after filing the European patent application but no later than thirteen months after the date of priority (see Rule 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derogations — oral proceedings language
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party to oral proceedings may use an official EPO language other than the language of the proceedings if they notify EPO at least two weeks before or provide interpreting into the language of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may also use official languages of Contracting States provided they make interpretation arrangements. EPO employees may use other official languages; the EPO may permit derogations, may provide interpretation at its own expense where necessary, and minutes record statements in the language used (translations entered in official language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non-official languages in taking evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses, experts or parties unable to express themselves adequately in EPO official languages or Contracting States' languages may use another language in taking of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the taking of evidence follows a party's request, the requesting party must provide interpretation into the language of the proceedings unless the EPO authorises interpretation into another official language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of language of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: On request by the applicant or proprietor and after consultation of other parties, the EPO may allow replacement of the language of proceedings by another official language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to a European patent application or European patent must be filed in the initial language of the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of European divisional application
rubrics_metrics.description: European divisional applications (or translations in cases under Article 14(2)) must be filed in the initial language of the proceedings for the earlier European patent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of translations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a translation of any document must be filed, the EPO may require a certificate that the translation corresponds to the original text within a period determined by EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the certificate in due time shall lead to the document being deemed not to have been received unless the Convention provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation time limits and fee reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limits for required translations and entitlement to fee reductions are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation under Article 14(2) must be filed within 3 months after filing but no later than 13 months after priority; translation under Article 14(4) must be filed within one month of filing the document (extended for notices of opposition/appeal). A reduction in filing/examination/opposition/appeal fees is allowed to those availing options in Article 14(2) and (4), fixed as a percentage in the Rules relating to Fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authenticity of translation
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining whether subject-matter extends beyond the content as filed, the EPO may, saving proof to the contrary, assume that the translation under Article 14(2) conforms to the original text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification to be used
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall use the International Classification: initially the 1954 classification until the Strasbourg Agreement (1971) enters into force, thereafter the Strasbourg Agreement classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of duties — first instance departments
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the EPO determines the number of Search, Examining and Opposition Divisions and allocates duties by reference to the international classification; he may decide classification where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President may allocate further duties to Receiving Section, Search, Examining, Opposition and Legal Divisions; may entrust non-qualified examiners with duties involving no technical/legal difficulty; may grant exclusive responsibilities to registries for fixing amounts of costs under Article 104(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of duties — second instance and designation of members
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties shall be allocated to Boards of Appeal and regular/alternate members designated before the start of each working year; members may serve on more than one Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An authority (President as Chairman, Vice-President responsible for appeals, Chairmen of Boards and three other elected members) decides these measures, requires quorum of at least five including the President/Vice-President and Chairmen of two Boards, decisions by majority with Chairman's casting vote; authority may amend measures during year and resolve allocation conflicts. Administrative Council may allocate duties under Article 134(8)(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of Procedure of Boards of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority designated for allocation shall adopt the Rules of Procedure of the Boards of Appeal; the Enlarged Board adopts its own Rules of Procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative structure of the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Examining and Opposition Divisions shall be grouped administratively into Directorates; Directorates, Legal Division, Boards of Appeal and administrative services grouped into Directorates-General, Receiving Section and Search Divisions grouped into a Directorate-General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Directorate-General directed by a Vice-President; appointment of Vice-Presidents decided by Administrative Council after consultation with the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proceedings where entitlement contested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party proves to the EPO that he has opened proceedings seeking a judgment that he is entitled to the grant of the European patent, the EPO shall stay the proceedings for grant unless the third party consents in writing to continuation; proceedings for grant may not be stayed before publication of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a final decision exists, EPO shall communicate resumption date; where decision is in favour of third party, resumption only after three months unless third party requests resumption. EPO may set a date to continue regardless of stage; time limits other than renewal fees are interrupted during suspension and resume with remaining time, but at least two months still to run after resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of withdrawal option when entitlement contested
rubrics_metrics.description: From the time a third party proves initiation of entitlement proceedings until EPO resumes proceedings, the European patent application and designation of any Contracting State may not be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing new European application by person adjudged entitled
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person adjudged by final decision to be entitled files a new European application under Article 61(1)(b), the original application is deemed withdrawn on the filing date of the new application for the designated Contracting States where the decision was taken or recognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing, search and designation fees for the new application must be paid within one month; designation fees may be paid up to expiry of the period in Article 79(2) if that period expires after this month. Time limits for forwarding applications under Article 77(3) and (5) are four months from actual filing date for the new application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial transfer of right by final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final decision adjudges a third party entitled to grant in respect of only part of the matter disclosed, Article 61 and Rule 15 apply mutatis mutandis to that part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original application may contain different claims/description/drawings for designated Contracting States where decision taken; where third party replaced previous proprietor for some states, patent as maintained in opposition may contain different claims/description/drawings for those states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation of the inventor shall be filed in the request for grant; if applicant is not inventor or sole inventor, designation shall be filed in a separate document stating family name, given names, full address and the statement referred to in Article 81, bearing applicant's or representative's signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO shall not verify accuracy of designation. If applicant is not inventor, EPO shall notify inventor a copy of the designation together with data in Article 128(5). Omissions or errors in notification cannot be invoked by applicant or inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of mention of the inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Person designated as inventor shall be mentioned as such in the published European patent application and patent specification; if not possible, at applicant/proprietor request the person shall be mentioned in copies not yet distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third party files a final decision requiring designation as inventor, the same measures apply; inventor may renounce title in writing to prevent measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of designation of an inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrect designation may not be rectified except upon request accompanied by consent of the wrongly designated person and, if request not filed by applicant/proprietor, by that party's consent; Rule 17 applies mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect entries in the Register or publications shall be corrected and corrected in all copies not yet distributed; cancellation treated similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering a transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Any transfer of a European patent application shall be recorded in the Register at the request of an interested party on production of the original or a certified copy of the instrument of transfer, or official documents verifying the transfer, or sufficient extracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO retains a copy of papers. Request is not deemed filed until administrative fee paid and may be rejected for failure to comply with conditions. No transfer effective vis-à-vis EPO until receipt and verification of papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering licences and other rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration rules of transfers apply mutatis mutandis to registration of grant/transfer of a licence, establishment/transfer of rights in rem in respect of a European patent application, and legal means of execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration can be cancelled upon request (not deemed filed until admin fee paid) supported by documents establishing lapse or proprietor consent; may be rejected if conditions not fulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special indications for registration of a licence
rubrics_metrics.description: A licence shall be recorded as an exclusive licence if applicant and licensee so require; a licence shall be recorded as a sub-licence where granted by a licensee whose licence is recorded in the Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of exhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must, within four months of filing the European patent application, file the certificate referred to in Article 55(2) issued at the exhibition by the authority responsible for industrial property protection, stating the invention was exhibited, opening date and date of first disclosure if different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate must be accompanied by identification of the invention, duly authenticated by the authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing — general provisions and receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: European patent applications may be filed directly or by post. The authority with which filed shall mark documents with date of receipt and issue without delay a receipt to the applicant including application number, nature and number of documents and date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed with a national office under Article 75(1)(b), that authority shall inform the EPO without delay of receipt and provide nature/date of receipt, application number and any priority date claimed. When EPO receives an application forwarded by a central industrial property office it shall inform the applicant indicating the date of EPO receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions for divisional applications (timing and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European divisional application may be filed at any time after receipt of the earlier application provided it is filed within the period prescribed in the Examining Division's first communication or the Examining Division later considers filing justified; or within two months following limitation invitation after Article 82 failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, description and drawings of earlier or divisional application shall relate only to matter for which protection is sought; where necessary to describe matter for another application, include a cross-reference. Filing, search and designation fees for each divisional must be paid within one month; designation fees may be paid up to expiry of Article 79(2) period if that period expires later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant — form and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for grant shall be filed on a form drawn up by the EPO; printed forms made available free by authorities under Article 75(1). The request shall contain a petition for grant, the title of the invention (clear, concise, technical; exclude fancy names and indicating claim categories), and name/address/nationality of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names of natural persons to be family name before given name(s); names of legal entities by official designations; addresses must satisfy postal delivery requirements and include relevant administrative units and house number if any. It is recommended to indicate telegraphic/teletype address and telephone number. If a representative is appointed, their name and address must be included (further content follows in next Rule text).
